common_meaning: Enjoyment, amusement or light-hearted pleasure; also (informally) enjoyable.
example: The game was a lot of fun, even though we lost.
rrgm_bridge: Fun is pleasure taken in the doing itself, not in what the doing achieves.
invariant_mi: Enjoyment arising from an activity valued for itself.

domain_entries.AFF: A light positive state of amusement and engagement. Parity line: whether a given system has this felt state is [UNK] under the Symmetry Rule; the behavioural markers can be described either way. Provisional domain.
domain_entries.REL: Shared fun builds bonds; play between people tests and strengthens trust.

count_condition: An activity or experience that is enjoyed for its own sake.
transfer_boundary: "Making fun of" someone means mocking them, which is not fun for its target. Fun for one party can be harm for another; the word does not settle whose experience counts.

common_meaning: Having previously been something, but no longer; or, as "the former", the first of two things mentioned.
example: She met her former teacher at the station.
rrgm_bridge: Former keeps the record of a past state while marking that it no longer holds; the history stays, the role ends.
invariant_mi: Previously holding a role or state that has since ended.

domain_entries.REL: A former partner, colleague or office-holder keeps a history with others while the role itself has ended.
domain_entries.LIN: "The former ... the latter" refers back to the first and second of two items.

count_condition: A person or thing that once had a role or state and no longer has it.
transfer_boundary: Former does not erase what was: the history remains true. A former role is not an ongoing claim.

common_meaning: A story or event recorded as moving images to be shown in a cinema or on a screen; also a thin layer, or the material once used in cameras.
example: We watched a film about the moon landing; a film of dust covered the shelf.
rrgm_bridge: A film fixes moving images in sequence so a story can be replayed for others.
invariant_mi: A recorded motion picture, or a thin covering layer.

domain_entries.DIG: Digital filmmaking and streaming have replaced most physical film.
domain_entries.REL: Films shape shared stories and how groups see each other.
domain_entries.PHY: A thin layer of a substance on a surface.

count_condition: A motion picture, or a thin coating.
transfer_boundary: A film based on true events is still a constructed story; it is free fiction aimed at the real, not a record.

common_meaning: After a long time or delay; also as the last in a series.
example: The bus finally arrived; finally, add the salt.
rrgm_bridge: Finally marks the end of a wait or the last step of a sequence.
invariant_mi: At the end, after delay or after other steps.

domain_entries.LIN: Signals relief after delay, or orders the last point in a list.

count_condition: An event at the end of a wait, or the last item in a sequence.
transfer_boundary: "Finally" can hint at impatience; it carries feeling as well as order.

common_meaning: Relating to a system of government in which power is divided between a central government and states or provinces.
example: Federal and provincial governments share responsibility for health.
rrgm_bridge: Federal names a structure of layered authority: a centre and member parts, each with its own powers.
invariant_mi: Of a union of self-governing units with a central government.

domain_entries.REL: Federalism divides power so that no single level holds all of it.
domain_entries.ECO: Federal budgets and taxes sit alongside state or provincial ones.

count_condition: A government or system made of member units under a shared central authority.
transfer_boundary: Which powers are federal and which are local varies by country and is often disputed.

common_meaning: A team game played with a ball; in most of the world, the game also called soccer; in North America, American or Canadian football.
example: They play football in the park on Sundays.
rrgm_bridge: Football names different games in different places; the word follows local custom.
invariant_mi: A team ball game, or the ball used in it.

domain_entries.REL: Football clubs carry strong local and national identities.
domain_entries.ECO: Professional football is a large industry.

count_condition: A ball game of the type called football locally, or its ball.
transfer_boundary: Which game "football" means depends on where the speaker lives.

common_meaning: Relating to money, especially how it is managed.
example: She sought financial advice.
rrgm_bridge: Financial names the domain of money held, owed and moved.
invariant_mi: Concerning money and its management.
count_condition: A matter concerning money.
transfer_boundary: Financial advice comes from someone with interests of their own; who pays the adviser matters.

common_meaning: Belonging to or coming from another country; also strange, or not belonging.
example: She speaks two foreign languages; a foreign object in the eye.
rrgm_bridge: Foreign marks something as from outside the speaker's own boundary.
invariant_mi: Of another country, or not belonging to the place where it is.

domain_entries.REL: Foreign is relative: everyone is foreign somewhere.
domain_entries.BIO: A foreign body is one the organism did not produce, which the immune system may attack.

count_condition: Something from outside a country or system.
transfer_boundary: Foreign is a position, not a property; it depends on where the speaker stands.

common_meaning: An enthusiastic supporter of a sport, team, person or activity; also a device that moves air.
example: She's a big fan of jazz; turn on the fan.
rrgm_bridge: A fan moves air; a fan keeps a following going.
invariant_mi: A devoted supporter, or a device that creates airflow.

domain_entries.REL: Fan communities share identity and enthusiasm; "fan" comes from "fanatic".
domain_entries.PHY: Rotating blades move air and cool by convection and evaporation.

count_condition: A supporter of something, or an air-moving device.
transfer_boundary: Being a fan of something does not make one a fair judge of it.

common_meaning: Causing laughter; also strange or odd.
example: The film was really funny; there's a funny smell.
rrgm_bridge: Funny marks a surprise that lands well, or one that unsettles.
invariant_mi: Amusing, or unexpectedly odd.

domain_entries.COG: Humour often turns on a sudden shift in expectation.

count_condition: Something amusing or strange.
transfer_boundary: Funny to the teller is not funny to the target; humour can wound.

common_meaning: The lower end of the leg, on which a person stands; also a unit of length (about 30 cm); also the bottom of something.
example: She hurt her foot; the tree is ten feet tall; at the foot of the hill.
rrgm_bridge: The foot is where a body meets the ground, and the base measure of length in older systems.
invariant_mi: The terminal part of the leg, a unit of length, or the base of something.

domain_entries.BIO: Bones, joints and muscles bearing body weight.

count_condition: A body part, a length of twelve inches, or a base.
transfer_boundary: Imperial and metric units are easy to mix up; conversions should be explicit.

common_meaning: Preferred above all others; as a noun, a person or thing most liked, or the competitor expected to win.
example: Blue is my favorite colour; the favorite won the race.
rrgm_bridge: Favorite ranks one thing first among many by preference.
invariant_mi: Most preferred, or most expected to win.

domain_entries.REL: Favoritism: treating one person better than others without fair reason.

count_condition: A thing or person ranked first in preference or expectation.
transfer_boundary: The favorite to win is not certain to win.

common_meaning: A cold-blooded animal that lives in water, breathes with gills and has fins; as a verb, to try to catch fish, or to search.
example: We caught three fish; she fished in her bag for keys.
rrgm_bridge: A fish is life shaped for water.
invariant_mi: An aquatic vertebrate with gills and fins, or to try to catch one.

domain_entries.BIO: Vast diversity; not a single evolutionary group.

count_condition: An aquatic gilled vertebrate, or the act of catching or searching.
transfer_boundary: "Fishing for compliments" means trying to get praise indirectly.

common_meaning: Completely; entirely.
example: The room is fully booked.
rrgm_bridge: Fully fills a measure to its limit.
invariant_mi: To the full extent.
count_condition: A state complete in extent.
transfer_boundary: Claims of "fully" checked or "fully" safe should be shown, not just stated.

common_meaning: The act of flying; also a journey by aircraft; also escape; also a set of stairs.
example: Our flight was delayed; the flight of refugees.
rrgm_bridge: Flight names movement through air, and escape from danger.
invariant_mi: Flying, an air journey, or escape.

domain_entries.BIO: Fight or flight: the body's rapid response to threat.

count_condition: Flying, a journey by air, an escape, or stairs.
transfer_boundary: Fleeing a threat is not cowardice; flight is a survival response.

common_meaning: The oily substance in animal bodies and some foods; as an adjective, having a lot of body fat, or thick.
example: Cut the fat off the meat; a fat book.
rrgm_bridge: Fat is the body's stored energy, and a word for thickness.
invariant_mi: Lipid tissue or substance, or thick in size.

domain_entries.BIO: Adipose tissue stores energy and insulates; dietary fats.
domain_entries.PEJ: Used as an insult to shame people for their bodies; the mechanism turns a body description into a moral judgement.

count_condition: Lipid substance, or something thick or large.
transfer_boundary: Body size is not a measure of health or worth on its own.

common_meaning: Known about by many people.
example: A famous painter.
rrgm_bridge: Famous measures how widely someone is known.
invariant_mi: Widely known.

domain_entries.REL: Fame brings attention, influence and loss of privacy.

count_condition: Someone or something widely known.
transfer_boundary: Famous is not the same as important or good.

common_meaning: Coming after the third; also one of four equal parts (a quarter).
example: She finished fourth.
rrgm_bridge: Fourth is the next step after the third.
invariant_mi: Ordinal of four, or a quarter.
count_condition: Position four, or one of four parts.
transfer_boundary: "The fourth estate" means the press.

common_meaning: Complete trust or confidence in someone or something; also strong belief in a religion.
example: I have faith in her; people of different faiths.
rrgm_bridge: Faith is trust held ahead of proof, which can be well or badly placed.
invariant_mi: Trust or belief not resting on proof.

domain_entries.MYT: Religious faith. Faith claims are held in their own domain.
domain_entries.REL: Good faith: honest intent in dealings.
domain_entries.COG: Faith differs from evidence-based belief in what it rests on.

count_condition: Trust in someone or something, or religious belief.
transfer_boundary: Good faith is about honesty, not certainty. Faith in a person can be tested by their conduct.

common_meaning: A popular style of clothes, hair or behaviour at a particular time; also a manner of doing something.
example: Short skirts were in fashion; in a strange fashion.
rrgm_bridge: Fashion is style that moves through a group for a time, then changes.
invariant_mi: A prevailing style, or a manner.
count_condition: A current style, or a way of doing.
transfer_boundary: What is in fashion is not better, only current; ideas have fashions too.

common_meaning: A sum of money saved or collected for a purpose; as a verb, to provide money for.
example: A pension fund; the study was funded by a charity.
rrgm_bridge: A fund is money set aside for a purpose, and funding chooses what goes forward.
invariant_mi: A reserve of money for a purpose, or to finance.

domain_entries.FOR: Who funds research is part of evaluating it.

count_condition: A pool of money, or the act of financing.
transfer_boundary: Funding a study does not make its result false, but it is a reason to check it.
